title: ValeVision AURA - The AURA Scene 1.0.0
description: A project's AURA scene (the 'aura file'): the model files AURA draws, copied into the project from ValeVision 3D's whitecard (method one) or, later, a SketchUp Painterly Scene Package (method two); the engine objects made from them; and the library assets stored in the project. One per project, <project>/ValeVision__AuraRender/UserData__AuraScene/<id>__AuraScene__.json, written by the AURA API (user data: collected to the PC, never pushed, never web-served). Placed assets and given materials are the drawing set's (AuraDrawingSet__Engine.Settings.Assets and .Materials, PainterlyNPR's own records); a material's '#Id' is this file's Object__Id. The folder, the lanes and the rules: AuraRender__SCHEMA__AuraScene__.md. Codified 30-Oct-2026.

AuraScene__ModelFiles.description: Every model file copied in, in the order the scene is built

AuraScene__Objects.description: The engine objects made from the Draw model files: every mesh node, in file order then node order. Ids never move

AuraScene__AssetFiles.description: The library assets stored in the project: one record per asset, however many placements use it

_rev.description: Written by the library writer (ValeShared__Library__ Na__Library__WriteJson) on every save: the 'someone else saved first' check

Schema.description: This contract, in AURA's app folder

Note.description: Anything a person should know about this scene

Method.description: ValeVision3dWhitecard: copies of ValeVision 3D's whitecard GLBs (method one). SketchUpScenePackage: ValeVision Cloud Sync's AURA export, read from Content__AuraScenePackages (method two, not built yet)

Folder.description: Where the model files were copied from, relative to the project: ValeVision3D/Content__3dModel__GlbFiles for method one

ListKey.description: The project record's list the folder was checked against: valeVision_ModelUrls for method one

Unlisted.description: In the folder but not in the list: copied all the same

Missing.description: In the list but not in the folder

SketchUpModelName.description: The SketchUp model the whitecard came from (the record's ValeVison3D__SketchUpCameraData.model_name)

ImportNumber.description: 1 for the first import, raised by each re-import

Import__ArchivedAs.description: The zip in Content__AuraScene__ModelFiles/00__Archive this import's files went into when the next import replaced them; null while they are current. Only the newest zip is kept, so an older entry names a zip that has gone

RotationDeg.description: About +Y, right-handed, applied first. A whitecard needs none: SketchUp's Front (-green) is already +Z

FrontFacing.description: The engine's front: the elevations are named from it

CentredOn.description: What the import put on the origin: the Focal model files' footprint, else the Architecture ones; Manual once set by hand. Changing the placement moves the building under every saved view

ModelFile__Id.description: The file name without the project's short name, 'TrueVision' and a leading number: the same after a re-import, so objects keep their file

ModelFile__FileName.description: The copy's name: its source's, byte for byte, in Content__AuraScene__ModelFiles

ModelFile__Use.description: Draw: its mesh nodes become objects. SourceLinework: SketchUp's own edges, kept for the engine's source linework (not built yet). Ignore: never drawn (ValeVision 3D's orbit helper cube)

ModelFile__Twin.description: The ModelFile__Id of its mesh or linework partner

ModelFile__Role.description: Its objects' starting role; null for a file that is not drawn

ModelFile__Sha256.description: The copy's, which is the source's: a different hash in ValeVision 3D means a newer whitecard

ModelFile__BoundsM.description: The file's contents in its own metres (+Y up), node transforms applied

Object__Id.description: The engine's Scene.Objects Id, '#Id' in a material assignment: from 1, never renumbered or reused. A re-import keeps an existing node's Id and gives a new node the next free one

Object__Node.description: The GLB node's name: how a re-import finds it again

Object__Mesh.description: The GLB mesh it draws: objects of one file with the same mesh are one shape, instanced

Object__PersistentId.description: SketchUp's persistent id, from an instanced component's node name (..._ID32059153): the second way a re-import finds it

Object__Category.description: The engine's category (Wall, Roof, Opening, Porch, Ground, ...): its pens and indication follow it

Object__Material.description: A material class Key (13__Scene__MaterialClasses), never Sky: the import's starting class, before any assignment in the drawing set

Object__Role.description: The engine's role (Architecture, Focal, Ground, Planting, Furniture, Context, Water, Boundary)

Object__Missing.description: Set by a re-import when the node has gone: the object stays, so its Id is never reused

AssetFile__GlbFile.description: The library's MOD file name, in Content__AuraScene__AssetFiles

AssetFile__DatFile.description: The library's DAT file name, beside it: the record as it was when copied

AssetFile__LibraryVersion.description: The pinned engine and library it was copied from

AssetFile__Instanced.description: true: every placement draws this one shape. false: each placement grows its own shape from its seed, from the same copy (the DAT's NewShapeEachPlop)
